key_insight: A graph neural network can learn cross-functional energy corrections to align heterogeneous DFT formation energies onto a common, higher-accuracy scale.
engineering_relevance: This enables legacy and multi-source PBE datasets to be upgraded toward r2SCAN-quality data for more reliable materials screening, stability prediction, and foundation model training.
method: Train on 380,190 paired PBE-r2SCAN structures from MatPES.
Use a structure-aware graph neural network (GPTFF) to predict residual energy shifts.
Convert PBE energies into r2SCAN-level formation energies via transfer learning.
evidence_signal: On MatPES, the model reduced PBE-to-r2SCAN conversion error to 14.3 meV/atom MAE, outperforming CHGNet at 18.2 meV/atom; the underlying PBE-r2SCAN discrepancy averages 107 meV/atom.
watch_item: Performance depends on the availability and representativeness of paired datasets, so extrapolation to unseen chemistries, functionals, or pseudopotential settings may be less reliable.
paper_title: Aligning Heterogeneous DFT Datasets: A Graph Neural Network Approach to Cross-Functional Formation Energies
